slides.texte_overlay:
quiet skills that make people
think you're a genius

summarising in one line

after any meeting, video or book, sum it up in one sentence. people who can squeeze a long idea into a short, clear line always sound brilliantly sharp.

asking the second why

when someone explains something, ask why one more time than feels polite. the second answer is where the real understanding is hiding, every single time.

knowing a bit of everything

i used to only know my own subject. learning a little about art, history and science every day changed how people see me, and now i can join any conversation.
slides.texte_sophia:
knowing a bit of everything

i used to only know my own subject. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app: art, history, science. people now think i know a bit about everything.

slides.texte_overlay:
remembering numbers

learn a few useful numbers by heart: distances, dates, populations. dropping one accurate figure into a conversation makes you sound instantly well informed.

saying i'm not sure

admit when you don't know, then say how you'd find out. confident uncertainty sounds far smarter than a guess, and people trust you so much more for it.
